question.text: Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) issued by the RBI on behalf of the government offer investors:

answer.text: Returns linked to gold price movements plus a fixed semi-annual coupon of 2.5% on the initial investment
Returns linked only to equity market performance with no fixed coupon
A fixed interest rate with no link to gold prices
Physical gold delivery at maturity instead of cash payment

explanation.text: The Logic: SGBs are gold-linked government securities. The tenor is 8 years with early encashment permitted after the fifth year. Investors receive a fixed semi-annual coupon of 2.5% on the initial investment, in addition to the maturity amount linked to the prevailing gold price. The Trap: SGBs are not linked to equity markets (option B). Returns are not purely fixed because they are linked to gold prices (option C). SGBs are settled in cash, not by physical gold delivery (option D). Note: The two return components — the 2.5% semi-annual coupon and the gold-price-linked redemption amount — together define an SGB's payoff.
